sample_unit: radiographs (11,980 with and 11,980 without model use) for documentation efficiency analysis
models_evaluated: workflow-integrated generative model for draft radiograph reports

links.outcome: Radiologist documentation time with versus without generative AI draft reports, plus peer-reviewed quality
links.effect: Model-assisted interpretations were faster (159.8 s vs 189.2 s; P = .02; 15.5% efficiency increase), with no difference in clinical accuracy (P = .41) or textual quality (P = .06) on peer review of 800 studies.
links.quote: Interpretations with model assistance (mean [SE], 159.8 [27.0] seconds) were faster than the baseline set of those without (mean [SE], 189.2 [36.2] seconds) (P = .02), representing a 15.5% documentation efficiency increase.

links.outcome: Prospective flagging of unexpected clinically significant pneumothorax on live radiographs
links.effect: The model flagged studies with clinically significant, unexpected pneumothorax with sensitivity of 72.7% and specificity of 99.9% among 97,651 studies screened.
links.quote: Moreover, the model flagged studies containing a clinically significant, unexpected pneumothorax with a sensitivity of 72.7% and specificity of 99.9% among 97 651 studies screened.

screen.reason: Prospective cohort study evaluating real clinical deployment of workflow-integrated generative AI draft reporting with human radiologist review, assessing efficiency, report quality, and acute finding flagging.

primary.practice: generative AI draft reporting with clinician review
